title: Cholangiohepatitis
desc: Amoxicillin plus a quinolone, with or without metronidazole; ursodiol, prednisolone and the supportive drugs (famotidine, Cerenia, mirtazapine). Includes anaesthesia premed and induction for liver biopsy.

meds.name: Amoxicillin
meds.desc: the amoxicillin half of the pair
meds.note: 10–20 mg/kg BID; the sheet's worked example uses 11 mg/kg BID.

meds.name: Zeniquin
meds.desc: quinolone — the target recommendation on this sheet

meds.name: Baytril
meds.note: Retinal toxicity is dose-dependent in cats — keep total daily enrofloxacin at or below 5 mg/kg/day.

meds.name: Chloramphenicol
meds.note: Warn owners about human exposure — gloves when handling, and it is not for a household with anyone who has a blood dyscrasia.

meds.name: Metronidazole
meds.desc: added to the amoxicillin and quinolone, not instead of them
meds.note: 7.5 mg/kg BID, often used alongside another antimicrobial because it kills anaerobes, penetrates bile and liver well, and has anti-inflammatory (cell-mediated immunity) and anti-endotoxic effects. Flagyl goes IN ADDITION to the amoxicillin and quinolone.

meds.name: Ursodiol
meds.note: 10–15 mg/kg per day. Do not use if there is a biliary obstruction.

meds.name: Prednisolone
meds.note: 2.2 mg/kg/day. Prednisolone rather than prednisone in cats.

meds.name: Butorphanol premed
meds.note: 0.2 mg/kg. Using the 10 mg/ml solution, divide the milligrams by 10 for the volume in ml.

meds.name: Buprenorphine premed
meds.note: 0.01 mg/kg. Using the 0.3 mg/ml solution, divide the milligrams by 0.3 for the volume in ml.

meds.name: Induction
meds.doseText: midazolam IV, followed by propofol TO EFFECT
meds.note: Induce with midazolam IV, then propofol titrated to effect. Check coagulation before biopsy.

notes.Antibiotic combination: Amoxicillin plus a quinolone is the base. Zeniquin 2.75 mg/kg SID and chloramphenicol 35 mg/kg BID are flagged on the sheet as the target recommendations.
notes.Why add metronidazole: Metronidazole 7.5 mg/kg BID is often used alongside another antimicrobial — it kills anaerobes, penetrates bile and liver well, and has anti-inflammatory (CMI) and anti-endotoxic effects. It goes IN ADDITION to the amoxicillin and quinolone, not in place of them.
notes.Enrofloxacin in cats: Retinal toxicity is dose-dependent — keep the total daily dose at or below 5 mg/kg/day, whether given once daily or split.
notes.Anaesthesia: Premed with butorphanol 0.2 mg/kg or buprenorphine 0.01 mg/kg. Induce with midazolam IV followed by propofol to effect.
notes.Appetite: These cats stop eating, and that risks hepatic lipidosis on top. Mirtazapine ¼ of a 7.5 mg tablet every other day, and consider a feeding tube early rather than late.

dischargeBlocks.title: What is going on
dischargeBlocks.text:
{name} has inflammation of the liver and the bile ducts. It makes cats feel sick, off their food, and sometimes jaundiced — the yellow tinge you may see in the gums, eyes or ears.

It responds to treatment, but the course is long. Several of these medications run for weeks.

dischargeBlocks.title: Eating is the most important thing
dischargeBlocks.text:
A cat that stops eating can develop a second liver problem on top of this one, and that is far harder to treat.

- Offer food little and often, warmed slightly so it smells stronger.
- Tell us straight away if {name} eats nothing for a whole day.
- If we dispensed an appetite stimulant, give it as directed.
- Never try to force food into {name}'s mouth — call us instead. If eating does not pick up we will talk about a feeding tube, which is a routine and very effective step.

dischargeBlocks.title: Giving the medication
dischargeBlocks.text:
There are several medications here and they have different schedules. Please follow the labels carefully, and finish the antibiotic course even once {name} seems well.

If {name} vomits a dose or you cannot get one in, call us rather than doubling up next time.

dischargeBlocks.title: Call us if you see
dischargeBlocks.text:
- Yellowing of the gums, the whites of the eyes, or the skin inside the ears
- Vomiting that does not stop, or repeated drooling
- {name} hiding, or not moving around normally
- Any bleeding, or bruising
- Refusing food for more than a day

dischargeBlocks.title: Follow up
dischargeBlocks.text:
We need to repeat {name}'s bloodwork on the schedule we discussed so we can see whether the liver values are improving and decide how long to continue.

Please keep those appointments — this is followed by the numbers, not by appearance alone.
